tagline: Zedd's divisive EDM anthem that animated five years of Worlds legends.
headline: Dismissed as too EDM in 2016, Zedd's Ignite has aged into the Worlds anthem that sounds like no other.
summary: Riot built the 2016 World Championship anthem with Grammy-winning producer Zedd, with Tim James on vocals, and premiered it on September 26, 2016 with an animated video that turns one legendary play from each Worlds between 2011 and 2015 into myth, including Faker eating broccoli on a throne. Many players compared it unfavourably with Warriors and one critic called it a generic EDM anthem, but Zedd opened the Staples Center final with a live orchestra and the video has since passed 105 million views. Ten years on, its most-liked comments call it the most unique Worlds song, it gave fans the 'Ignite uses Smite' joke, and Zedd has kept working with Riot.

story.heading: A Grammy winner for Worlds
story.body:
By 2016 the Worlds anthem was a tradition: Imagine Dragons' *Warriors* in 2014, then Nicki Taylor's *Worlds Collide* in 2015. For the sixth World Championship, which toured San Francisco, Chicago and New York before a final at Los Angeles' Staples Center, Riot made a sharp turn and called Zedd, the Grammy-winning electronic producer. The reveal was a slow burn. On September 23 the LoL Esports account posted a GIF of Kha'Zix watching an explosion, with Zedd's logo laid over the Worlds emblem, and Zedd answered with a date: 9/26.

*Ignite* was written by Anton Zaslavski (Zedd), Antonina Armato, Tim James and TAS. Zedd produced and mixed it, Rock Mafia handled vocal production, and Tim James, who had also sung Zedd's *True Colors*, provided the vocals. Riot composer Sebastien Najand handled the orchestral arrangement and production. The title is a double meaning every player would catch: Ignite is also the summoner spell that sets an enemy on fire. Interscope released the song as a single, *Ignite (2016 League of Legends World Championship)*, the day after Riot's video.

story.heading: Five Worlds in under four minutes
story.body:
The video is a highlight reel turned into a fever dream. Riot's Kien Lam published a breakdown of the stories behind it, and Riot posted a companion video that sets each animated scene beside the original broadcast footage.

The five stories run in order. **2011:** in the first-ever Worlds final, aAa's YellOwStaR walks his Ashe into a Brand stun, watches from a grey screen, then answers with an arrow fired across the whole map. **2012:** the underdog Taipei Assassins take on Korea's Azubu Frost in what Riot framed as David against Goliath, and Toyz's Orianna chases down and reels in a fleeing Shen. **2013:** TSM's TheOddOne, the team's 'General', throws his Elise into OMG's Baron attempt and steals it with one last Smite, knowing he won't survive. **2014:** sOAZ's Rumble Teleports into OMG's base to start a Fnatic backdoor, and Loveling's Kog'Maw keeps the Nexus alive with a sliver of health. **2015:** Faker's Ryze closes out the final against the KOO Tigers, and the video seats him on a throne.

The final act brings it all together. Faker steps off his throne, the champions from every story charge together, and the camera lands on the Summoner's Cup under the lasers of a Worlds 2016 arena. Then it cuts to a young player at a sunlit bedroom desk and a title card: *Summon your champion*.

story.heading: Win or die: the backlash
story.body:
*Ignite* started fast. Rolling Stone counted more than three million views within a day of release. But it was being measured against *Warriors*, which already had nearly 60 million views. The Zedd fan wiki notes that many League players received it negatively and compared it unfavourably with Imagine Dragons' anthem. Music Times heard vintage Zedd in the gritty electro drops but found the vocals a bit cheesy. Player.One went further, calling it a generic EDM anthem and pointing readers to JonTron's 2011 parody *The Leagüe and I* instead.

The song had defenders from the start. We Rave You called it a future-house tune with a drop big enough for gamers and electronic music lovers alike. One much-liked comment from 2016 admitted the song improved with every rewatch.

story.heading: Staples Center, October 29, 2016
story.body:
Three days before the final, Riot released *Ignite: Finals Remix*, which added Najand as a co-writer and credited him with orchestral arrangement, mixing and additional production. On October 29 Zedd opened the final at Staples Center with a new remix of *Ignite*, backed by a live orchestra. EDMTunes described him being slowly revealed in a booth inside giant walls of animated graphics, lights and vivid colour. A few days later he shared the performance as *Ignite (Live from Staples Center)*.

Nearly 20,000 fans were in the arena, 43 million unique viewers watched online (14.7 million at the peak), and SK Telecom T1 beat Samsung Galaxy 3–2 to become the first team to win three World Championships. Faker was named tournament MVP. A month after the video put him on a throne, with Riot's write-up saying he welcomed any new challengers, he defended it.

story.heading: Broccoli, Smite and Championship Zed
story.body:
The video gave the community plenty of jokes. The best known is Faker's broccoli. Rolling Stone explained that the shot recreates him keeping a promise to a fan by eating a broccoli floret after SKT's 2015 title, and "INTENSE BROCCOLI ACTION" was an early comment favourite. At 1:17 there is a second running gag: Tim James sings "and ignite" just as the animation brings a Smite down on Baron, and fans have been pointing out the mismatch for years.

The timing of the launch fed the jokes too. Championship Zed, that year's Worlds skin, went on sale the same day the video premiered, and commenters quickly noticed Riot pairing Zedd with Zed, just as Imagine Dragons had arrived alongside Championship Shyvana. Another favourite: "2016 = win or die. 2017 = legends never die." One of the video's most-liked comments complains about feeling baited every time the beat suddenly stops.

story.heading: Aged like fine wine
story.body:
Critics still put *Ignite* near the bottom of their Worlds rankings: 8th of 11 at ONE Esports, 10th of 11 at Dot Esports and 10th of 12 at Esports Insider. Yet their write-ups agree on what makes it stand out. Dot Esports says it goes in a completely different direction from every other Worlds song, Esports Insider says its overtly EDM nature earns it a bad rap, and ONE Esports calls it the pick for EDM fans while praising a video full of iconic Worlds moments. Years of YouTube comments tell a softer story: "still the most unique Worlds song 5 years later" and "this one was ahead of its time" are among its most-liked comments.

The numbers hold up as well. The video has about 105.7 million views, almost three times *Worlds Collide*'s 36.3 million and just ahead of Linkin Park's 2024 anthem *Heavy Is the Crown*. The Finals Remix adds another 13.9 million, and the single has passed 80 million Spotify streams. The people behind it stayed close to Riot. Zedd worked with Riot on VALORANT's *Spectrum* weapon skins and debuted his remix of Grabbitz's *Die For You* at the VALORANT Champions 2021 finals opening ceremony. Najand, who arranged *Ignite*'s orchestra, also co-wrote K/DA's *POP/STARS* and *GODS*, NewJeans' Worlds 2023 anthem.

whyItMatters: Riot handed the Worlds anthem to a Grammy-winning electronic producer, a sharp turn from the rock and orchestral anthems before it that critics still single out as the series' outlier.

Its video recreated five legendary pro plays from 2011 to 2015 (YellOwStaR's arrow, Toyz's Orianna, TheOddOne's Baron steal, Fnatic's backdoor and Faker's Ryze), and Riot published a companion video and article showing the real footage behind each one.
It soundtracked the Staples Center final, which Zedd opened with a live orchestra, where SKT became the first three-time world champions with Faker, the king of the video's last act, as MVP.
The official video has about 105.7M views, roughly 2.9× the previous year's Worlds Collide, and the Finals Remix adds 13.9M more.
It gave League some lasting jokes: Faker's broccoli, a Smite where the lyric says 'ignite', and Zedd arriving the same day as Championship Zed.
Its makers stayed in Riot's orbit: Zedd later made VALORANT's Spectrum skins and a Champions 2021 remix, and Riot composer Sebastien Najand, who arranged its orchestra, co-wrote POP/STARS and GODS.

communityMoments.title: Kha'Zix lights the fuse
communityMoments.description: LoL Esports teased the anthem with a GIF of Kha'Zix watching an explosion, with Zedd's logo laid over the Worlds emblem. Zedd confirmed it on Twitter with just a date: 9/26.

communityMoments.title: The plays behind the video
communityMoments.description: Riot published Kien Lam's breakdown of the five Worlds stories in the video, plus a companion video setting each animated scene next to the original broadcast footage.

communityMoments.title: Zedd, meet Championship Zed
communityMoments.description: Championship Zed went on sale the same day Ignite premiered, and a popular comment on the video pointed out the pattern: Imagine Dragons got Championship Shyvana, Zedd got Championship Zed.

communityMoments.title: INTENSE BROCCOLI ACTION
communityMoments.description: The shot of Faker eating broccoli on his throne, which recreates his promise to a fan after the 2015 title, became the video's signature meme, and broccoli jokes still fill its comments.

communityMoments.title: "Use JonTron's song instead"
communityMoments.description: The backlash peaked with Player.One calling Ignite a generic EDM anthem and pointing readers to JonTron's 2011 parody The Leagüe and I instead.

communityMoments.title: The Finals Remix
communityMoments.description: Three days before the final, Riot released an alternate version with orchestral arrangement, mixing and additional production by Riot composer Sebastien Najand.

communityMoments.title: Zedd opens the Worlds final
communityMoments.description: Before SKT and Samsung Galaxy took the stage at Staples Center, Zedd played a new remix of Ignite with a live orchestra, surrounded by animated visuals.

communityMoments.title: Live from Staples Center
communityMoments.description: Zedd shared his own video of the performance, titled Ignite (Live from Staples Center). LoL Esports later posted a 360-degree recording of the finals opening ceremony.

communityMoments.title: "Ignite!" *uses Smite*
communityMoments.description: At 1:17 the vocal hits 'and ignite' just as TheOddOne's Elise brings Smite down on Baron. The mismatch is one of the most-liked running jokes in the video's comments.

communityMoments.title: Zedd returns for VALORANT Champions
communityMoments.description: Five years after Ignite, Zedd and Grabbitz debuted Zedd's remix of the VALORANT Champions anthem Die For You at the 2021 finals opening ceremony.

communityMoments.title: "Ahead of its time"
communityMoments.description: The verdict has softened. Some of the video's most-liked later comments call Ignite the most unique Worlds song and say it was ahead of its time.

keyMoments.label: 2011: Ashe on the ruins
keyMoments.description: The first story begins. Ashe, YellOwStaR's pick for aAa in the first Worlds final, draws her bow as a blazing Brand bears down on her.

keyMoments.label: Grey screen
keyMoments.description: The player behind the Ashe stares in shock, clicks frantically, then tumbles backward, mirroring the stun that killed his Ashe.

keyMoments.label: 2012: David and Goliath
keyMoments.description: The Taipei Assassins sit at their PCs as a towering ice-blue giant rises behind them. Riot's write-up framed their final against Korea's Azubu Frost as David against Goliath.

keyMoments.label: 2013: The spider's descent
keyMoments.description: Elise closes in on Baron Nashor, setting up TheOddOne's Baron steal against OMG.

keyMoments.label: One last charge from the General
keyMoments.description: TheOddOne, in his TSM shirt, salutes and dives into the red sky, a do-or-die leap that mirrors the steal itself.

keyMoments.label: First drop: Smite!
keyMoments.description: Elise raises a claw and a bolt crashes onto Baron as the vocal lands on 'and ignite'. Fans love to point out that the spell on screen is Smite.

keyMoments.label: YellOwStaR's redemption arrow
keyMoments.description: Crowned Ashe takes aim and fires a glowing arrow that streaks across the map, the 2011 shot from Riot's breakdown.

keyMoments.label: The beat cuts out
keyMoments.description: The music drops to near silence for about two seconds before the second verse builds back up.

keyMoments.label: 2014: sOAZ's Teleport
keyMoments.description: Rumble's mech stalks through a burning landscape, a green Teleport flares, and the mech marches on OMG's Nexus to start Fnatic's backdoor attempt.

keyMoments.label: Defending the Nexus
keyMoments.description: A uniformed player is swallowed by flames and lava, one hand reaching out, as OMG's base burns.

keyMoments.label: 2015: The Demon King
keyMoments.description: Faker appears in his SK Telecom T1 jacket, then takes his seat on a towering throne.

keyMoments.label: The broccoli
keyMoments.description: Faker eats broccoli on his throne, recreating his promise to a fan after SKT's 2015 title and creating the video's most-quoted meme.

keyMoments.label: Faker leaves the throne
keyMoments.description: Faker steps down from the throne, and the champions from every story charge together as the final drop hits.

keyMoments.label: The Summoner's Cup
keyMoments.description: The Summoner's Cup stands under lasers on the Worlds 2016 stage, and the camera pulls back over the crowd and out over a neon arena.

keyMoments.label: Summon your champion
keyMoments.description: The video ends with a young player at a sunlit bedroom desk, a hand on the mouse, and the title card 'Summon your champion'.

keyMoments.label: Finals Remix: the long drop
keyMoments.description: Over a still image of the Summoner's Cup and the Worlds 2016 crest, the remix hits its first long full-power drop, which runs to about 1:29.

keyMoments.label: Finals Remix: the finale
keyMoments.description: The last and longest full-intensity stretch begins and carries the remix to about 3:15.

featuredClip.description: The first drop: Elise raises a claw, a Smite bolt crashes onto Baron Nashor as the vocal lands on 'and ignite', and the scene cuts to the Taipei Assassins as an ice-blue giant's fist lunges at them.
